cost: O(V+E) time and auxiliary space, including adjacency, vertex state, edge stack, labels and output. Each adjacency entry is consumed once, each non-loop identity pushed and popped once, and canonicalization scans identities once without sorting. Validation is O(E) before V adjacency allocation. All counts/indexes fit materialized vectors. Explicit stacks avoid recursive DFS.
description: Validate endpoints in edge order, u before v, through bridges::adjacency. Partition non-loop edge identities by the equivalence relation generated by membership in a common simple cycle; parallel edges form a two-edge cycle. Each loop and each bridge is a singleton. Isolates produce nothing. Return sorted IDs in blocks ordered by minimum ID.

inverse: For domain D and Result space Y let R be the stated exact forward relation. The behavior complement is (D x Y) minus R, including wrong memberships/counts, malformed canonical outputs, wrong errors and wrong precedence. This is a specification complement; correspondence to source is partial and is not a proof.

For partition P, retain all vertex counts and ordered endpoint assignments whose cycle-equivalence classes, singleton loops and bridges equal P. A singleton does not distinguish a loop from a bridge, and no endpoint is uniquely recoverable. Error fibers fix only the first invalid endpoint and preceding valid endpoints.
limitations: Finite checks do not prove unrestricted correctness.
Partial syntax has no macro expansion or semantic resolution.
Allocation failure and executable approximation profiles are outside this model.
state: Finite materialized ordered graphs and machine-sized indices, fixed input, successful allocation. Observations are returned Result values; allocator failure and wall-clock timing are outside the relation.
